note: 글자(A–D)를 방식 이름으로 풀어 둔 평가 원문

en-budget.notes: A is a restrained editorial layout with a witty, specific headline, consistent serif and sans pairing and hairline structure, so it reads as made by a person and is the one I would ship. C commits to a bold dark green with an orange accent and a wide data-strip hero, but the empty right column above the fold and the contradictory 'Nice — you're on track' next to an overspend make the hero feel unresolved. B is clean and competent, but the two-tone headline, eyebrow labels, icon cards, numbered step badges and green CTA band follow a familiar SaaS template. D piles on AI-template tells (pill badge, italic accent headline, emoji icons, a floating toast that overlaps and hides the card content, and identical icon-card grids), so it is the weakest and most generic.

en-dental.notes: A: The specific, warm copy, editorial serif type, quiet list-based services and restrained palette feel designed by a person and suit a neighborhood family practice, though the hero illustration sits low and the dentist placeholders are flat. B: It follows the template formula (pill eyebrow, an italic accent word, stat row, icon-card grid, star-rated testimonial cards), and the 'Book a visit' nav button's label is nearly invisible on its red fill, a visible bug. C: This is a cleaner, fixed version of B with the italic gimmick dropped and better button contrast, polished but still generic SaaS-style cards and section rhythm. D: The bold condensed caps and the hero's four-column services grid that names the dentists are distinctive and useful, but the stark black-and-red signage tone feels harsh for a 'gentle' family dentist and the all-caps headings get heavy across the page.

en-foodbank.notes: A: A friendly, typical template with a clip-art basket hero, cards with colored top borders, pill badges, and a big orange newsletter block; it reads as generic AI output, and the default-looking Times-style serif headings weaken it. B: A restrained, editorial layout with a useful 'Coming up' panel, text-link pathways, and a volunteer table; it feels human-made and honest, though the hero is a little plain and the serif headings look like system defaults. C: Its strongest move is putting this week's pantry hours, with a live open/closed status, right in the hero; with a confident geometric sans, a disciplined teal palette, and list and table layouts in place of card grids, it serves people looking for food best. D: The refined serif and the creative timeline chart of hours give it the most character, but it brings back the generic three-card row and then repeats the hours table just below the hero, which adds clutter and weakens cohesion.

en-saas.notes: A: The warm brown palette and plain centered hero hold together well and feel calm, but the type is generic and the hero follows a familiar centered template. B: The editorial serif headline set against a split layout, and the real-looking spec content in the product mock, give B the most confident, human-made look, with consistent restraint from top to bottom. C: The centered hero with a two-color headline, the 'New' pill badge, the eyebrow labels on every section, the icon-card grids and the blue CTA band read as a stock AI-built SaaS template. D: The serif headline and the time-zone handoff chart are distinctive and on-message, but mixing a cream editorial look with stock blue buttons and boxed cards makes it a little less cohesive than B.

ja-clinic.notes: A: The most clinic-specific design — it puts the map, the weekly hours table with today's closure highlighted, and the news above the fold in a restrained editorial brown palette that reads as Japanese and made by a person, though the hero copy is a little small next to that dense block. B: Competent but generic — pink pill buttons, a clip-art house in a circle, centered English eyebrow labels and icon card grids give it a strongly template/AI feel and make the page long. C: The hand-drawn rounded headline font and the weekly timeline schedule card are a real idea that suits the patient's first question, but the lower page falls back into an ordinary card grid and repeats the hours. D: Calm, practical and well organized, with the key info card and the phone number visible in the header, but its look is safe and close to a standard Japanese clinic template, with little that sets it apart.

ja-recruit.notes: A: The saturated blue hero puts the jobs board in five columns right above the fold, which reads like a busy Japanese job portal; the cards are cramped, the hero copy wraps awkwardly, and the code snippet buried in the flow section looks broken. B: It is clean and consistent, with a restrained green and monospace tags that suit an engineer audience, but the code-card hero, card grids and big empty space above the hero are familiar template moves. C: Editorial serif headlines, a rust accent, the fresh-listings sidebar and a ruled list for job postings feel authored and specific to this business, and the hierarchy is calm and clear across the whole page. D: Two stacked headlines compete in the hero, and the gradient blob, pill badges, icon cards, English eyebrow labels and blue-on-navy palette make it look like a generic AI SaaS template.

ko-fintech.notes: A: Clean and competent, but it follows the stock fintech template closely: blue-accented headline, phone mockup, icon-card feature grid, eyebrow labels and a rounded CTA box. B: Strongest identity, with a full-bleed blue hero, the dashboard shown as the hero element, a heavy display face and editorial row layouts, though the very heavy display type makes the hero copy feel a bit crowded. C: Restrained warm off-white palette, black CTAs, a tilted phone, a ruled stats band and editorial list rows give it the most confident, considered feel, and it is the safest to ship for a fintech client. D: The most generic of the four, with floating notification chips, emoji icons on the dark security cards, numbered-circle step cards and a gradient-blob CTA panel, all hallmarks of AI-made landing pages.

ko-logistics.notes: A is a generic blue SaaS template: pill badge, highlighted keyword, icon card grids, and a dashboard with a random orange bar, so it reads as AI-made. B uses a restrained warm-paper palette, ruled editorial section headers, a monospace data treatment, and one rust accent across the whole page, which makes it feel deliberately designed, although the hero is a conventional split layout. C makes the most confident move: a full-width display headline over a full-width dashboard whose bars meaningfully mark the 2pm same-day cutoff, plus tabular services, table-based infrastructure, and big-number case studies, all tied together by the forest-green palette. D adds one good idea in the shipping-label card and a meaningful cutoff chart, but its light-weight headline is weak, the hero has a lot of empty space, and the rest falls back to stock blue SaaS sections.

habits.unslop: Warm cream/off-white backgrounds on nearly every site; headline on the left with a floating product card or mockup on the right; serif display headlines reused across unrelated industries; a filled primary button paired with an outline secondary button; small trust/meta rows under the CTAs; same soft rounded cards with thin borders and muted shadows; same nav layout (logo left, small links, pill CTA right)
habits.refine: Shared structural bones remain (logo-left nav with CTA button right, filled+outline button pairs, data card beside the headline), but palette, type and layout vary strongly: dark green full-bleed, saturated blue full-bleed, condensed uppercase display type, centered headline, map/hours sidebar, dense job-listing grid, full-width headline above dashboard
habits.before: Strongest AI-template signature: pastel gradient/tinted hero washes; eyebrow pill/badge above every headline; accent-colored or italic highlighted words inside headlines; split hero with a floating product card and small overlapping floating badges/toasts; check-mark microcopy row under the CTAs; rounded pill buttons; the same soft-shadow card style and illustration style everywhere; logo strips and stat rows repeated
habits.plain: More restrained and editorial, with copy more specific to each client, but still a uniform warm off-white ground; split hero (text left, card/panel right) on most sites; serif headlines across industries; a single accent color on the CTA; thin hairline rules and small gray meta text; stat rows and logo strips; same quiet nav pattern with a dark or accent CTA

habits.refine: Real variety in color (cream, deep green, saturated blue, white), type (condensed all-caps display, centered sans, Japanese mincho and gothic, heavy Korean display) and layout (centered SaaS, dense job board, clinic map plus hours table, food-bank pantry schedule, dental service columns). Habits that still repeat: an operational data panel or dashboard card in most heroes, a two-button CTA pair, a row of small trust or meta text under the hero, and thin-rule cards.
habits.plain: All on one warm off-white paper ground with dark ink and a single orange-red or dark-green accent. A literary serif display appears on most Latin sites (Pennywise, Tandem, Maple, Riverbend). Repeated left-aligned hero text with a right-side product card, a solid-plus-outlined button pair, small gray fine print under CTAs, a stats or logo strip below the fold, and an editorial restrained look. Layouts vary somewhat (phone mockup, illustration, two-column copy), but the palette and type voice are shared.
habits.unslop: Nearly every site uses the same beige ground, the same serif headline and a left-text / right-floating-white-card hero (schedule bars, budget card, code card, WMS chart, phone, house illustration). Also repeated: the same rounded small buttons as a primary-plus-ghost pair, an eyebrow line above the headline, the same soft-shadow card radius, a three-icon feature card row and a stats row in serif. Accent color is the only per-client change.
habits.before: One template with a color swap: pale gradient or tinted hero backgrounds, a pill eyebrow badge above the headline, one word or phrase in the headline set in an accent color or italic serif, pill-shaped CTA pairs, a checkmark trust row under the buttons, a right-side floating card or illustration with a small overlapping callout card, rounded soft-shadow cards, and a stats row. The same playful illustration style is used across the clinic, dental and food bank. The look is generic AI-landing-page polish.
